doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Students who were ear learners and the Jazzanians
summary: His students were all self-taught; his ethnomusicology background shaped his respect for how they played.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you benefit from your students as well as they benefitted from you? I’m thinking about my own experience of working with musicians who may not have come through what we call a schooled music education, that they were ear learners and learned on the gig. And I wonder if you had students like that and what you might have gained from that association?

I didn’t have students like that — some students like that — they were all like that. Every one of them. And I gained a huge amount from that, of course. But also I was that was myself, surprisingly. I wasn’t the product of a jazz program. You know I didn’t go to Berklee or Indiana University or North Texas State. The degree to which I had formal music training at a university level was in ethnomusicology. So I was very open to and curious about what processes enabled these musicians to be as good as they all were anyway, without the sort of background that you’re talking about. And I knew, because they all told me this, that what they wanted to learn was what you got from formal education. There’s a myth in some circles that whether they’re talking about me or some years later other university people were imposing our standards, our processes on people who were already musical and thereby depriving them of something — not at all, it certainly wasn’t my way and I don’t know of other instances either. They came to university not to learn what they could already do, but you know what I mean?

So you know if you listen to The Jazzanians or — do you know about — yeah, you would know about The Jazzanians. But what you hear is, you know, tremendous feel, great coherence in the rhythm section, a completely different approach to soloing, you hear borderline but somehow not to my ear anyway, I’m acclimatized to what would be intonation issues.
